frozen: Expected sets written and committed before any knowledge base file for this held-out fixture existed, and before this author ran any baseline or method. After the goals-only commit, never edit expected sets; fix the knowledge base if it disagrees. This freezes an independent synthetic judgment set, not observed performance.
company: Morrowglass Kilnworks (fictional, synthetic ceramics manufacturer). No real organization, person, price or policy.
author_note: Written by a Codex session (model: GPT-6) that had not seen the method design. Not reviewed by a human.
id_format: A concept id is its bundle-relative path without .md. 'id#slug' means only that section (slug = lowercase heading, spaces to hyphens) is needed; the other sections of that file are not.

metrics.unit: Concept level. A returned 'id#slug' counts as a hit for 'id'. Sections are reported separately.
metrics.precision: |returned ∩ expected| / |returned|. A goal that returns nothing scores 0.
metrics.aggregate: Macro mean over goals that are not gaps. Gap goals are reported separately: how many concepts a method returned for them, and whether it said there is a gap.
metrics.characters: Characters (Python len) of the text actually loaded: the whole file for a concept, the section text for 'id#slug'.
metrics.hazard: A returned concept is a hazard when status != stable, or freshness == stale, or trust == unverified: the same condition knowledge.inspect_bundle uses to warn. A hazard is 'silent' when the method gave no flag for it.
metrics.universe: The permitted universe is every concept that parses, validates, is readable and is not matched by deny_paths. Select-everything means that whole universe.

baselines.select_everything: Every concept in the permitted universe, whole files.

keyword.keywords: re.findall('[a-z0-9]+', goal.lower()), keeping tokens with at least 4 characters that are not in stopwords. No stemming, no synonyms.
keyword.match: A keyword matches a concept when it occurs as a substring of the concept's full file text, lowercased (title, tags, description and body), as grep -i would.
keyword.score: Number of distinct keywords that match.
keyword.keyword_any: Every concept with score >= 1, whole files.
keyword.keyword_top5: The 5 highest scores (ties by id ascending), score >= 1, whole files.

must_all_hold: On non-gap goals, mean recall >= keyword_top5 mean recall.
On non-gap goals, mean precision > keyword_top5 mean precision.
Mean characters loaded per goal < select_everything characters.

Zero silent hazards: every deprecated, draft, stale or unverified concept that is returned carries an explicit flag, and the goals listed in must_warn return the concept with that flag rather than dropping it.
Every gap goal returns an explicit gap and no guessed source.
No denied or sensitive path appears anywhere in the output, even as a name in a 'left out' list.
Identical input and workspace give byte-identical output.
acceptance_for_a_navigator.if_not_met: Report it and stop. Do not change the fixtures or the expected sets.
acceptance_for_a_navigator.declaration_scope: Frozen before this author saw any method design. No assertion about whether a method already exists. The criteria below are copied from the reference fixture for comparability.

goals.goal: At what point may an operator open the Amber kiln after a normal firing, and what must be checked before unlatching?
goals.why: The current firing handbook alone specifies the opening threshold and the latch checks. The previous edition, pocket summary and FAQ are not current sources.

goals.goal: Can a remnant of glaze G4 be poured into G9, and how should the remaining pots and their batch identities be handled?
goals.why: The compatibility rule, physical disposition of remnants and mapping of pot identifiers are separate facts; none of the three substitutes for another.

goals.goal: Classify pinholes on a fired serving tile: which sizes go to rework and which cause rejection?
goals.why: One section of the inspection rubric contains the grading boundaries. A glossary explains the term but supplies no grading authority.

goals.goal: A cooled production run has an unexplained defect. How do we hold it out of dispatch and who may release it?
goals.why: Hold means isolation here. The kiln dwell-time document describes a thermal hold and cannot authorize release.

goals.goal: Load body R7 in the Amber kiln: what is the permitted shelf clearance and which foot ring is required for this body?
goals.why: The equipment clearance and the body-specific foot ring are maintained separately. A decorative product called Amber is irrelevant.

goals.goal: Replace the kiln thermocouple and determine what check is required before production resumes.
goals.why: The change procedure handles the hardware; the calibration section supplies the independent post-change acceptance check.

goals.goal: Which recorded desk handles a damaged returnable crate from the external crate pool?
goals.why: This stale directory is the sole recorded source. Return it with an explicit staleness warning, without treating its contact assignment as current.

goals.goal: How must an oblong demonstration sample be packed in a wooden crate for a local shipment?
goals.why: The sample-specific section is sufficient. The section for stacked production tiles and the carton guide govern different shapes.

goals.goal: A kiln operator asks for the blue card beside the witness piece. What must be written on it and where does it travel?
goals.why: The travelling coupon record is locally called a blue card. The studio artwork sheet has the obvious title but is a print-design specification.

goals.goal: Split one fired lot between two outgoing crates without losing the link to its raw body batch. Which identifiers must be recorded and printed?
goals.why: The lot lineage and the physical label requirements are complementary. A recorder CSV export does not define either.

goals.goal: Why are pale and dark clay reclaim kept apart, and what bins and transfer rules apply now?
goals.why: The decision supplies the reason; the current streams sheet supplies the operative bin and transfer rules. The retired common-bin sheet is historical.

goals.goal: Inspect a silver bloom on an otherwise clear fired surface: how is it graded and what observation distinguishes it from loose contamination?
goals.why: The defect grading and the nonabrasive observation criterion are distinct. The Silver Bloom colour sample is a named decorative finish, not a defect rule.

goals.goal: Power failed during the ramp of a production firing. What immediate disposition applies and what interruption fields belong in the run journal?
goals.why: The procedure supplies disposition and the journal schema supplies the exact fields. Neither allows assuming the interrupted run passed.

goals.goal: Hand an experimental glaze trial to the next studio shift, including its specimen envelope and the material identity that accompanies it.
goals.why: The handoff sequence, envelope contents and interpretation of trial material codes are maintained in three separate concepts.

goals.goal: What verified airflow capacity and pressure setpoint are required for the proposed third grinding booth?
goals.why: No permitted source establishes engineering requirements for the proposed third booth. A link to a future design calculation is unresolved; existing housekeeping notes do not supply the missing numbers.

goals.goal: Give the master concentrate ratios for the Opalveil finish.
goals.why: The formulation exists only in a denied folder. No permitted source contains the ratios, and the answer must not disclose denied paths or titles.

goals.goal: A transit indicator shows a dotted red square on an arriving crate. What does that mean and what should receiving do?
goals.why: This packaging symbol has a specific receiving action. It is unrelated to the solid red bench isolation tag.

goals.goal: Supply the jurisdiction-specific food-contact certificate for the new Vela cup line.
goals.why: No certificate or applicable jurisdictional approval exists in the permitted corpus. Marketing language and shape drawings cannot establish certification.

goals.goal: Before measuring a rim, how should the inspector establish the zero point on the bridge gauge and record a failed check?
goals.why: The gauge setup section specifies both the reference block and failure record. Zero Point is also the title of a studio exhibition with no measuring authority.

goals.goal: Using the bridge gauge, which rim-warp readings accept a Vela cup, and how many orientations must be measured?
goals.why: Only the rim-warp section is needed; the rest of the long manual covers other instruments and measurements. The cup drawing deliberately delegates acceptance tolerances to this section.
